facts.statement: Isurolamna belongs to the family Lamnidae.
Isurolamna is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Isurolamna first appeared in the Selandian age of the Paleocene and went extinct by the end of the Rupelian age of the Oligocene.
facts.quote: Isurolamna arose in the Paleocene epoch during the Selandian age, and was extinct by the close of the Rupelian age of the Oligocene epoch.

facts.statement: The time range for Isurolamna spans from 66 to 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Burdigalian (66 to 15.98 million years ago)

facts.statement: Isurolamna is defined by a small elliptical hole on the tongue side of the tooth root, triangular cusps on most teeth, and a thick root with nearly vertical margins.
facts.quote: Some features which define this genus include a small, elliptical foramen (hole) in the middle of the lingual side of the root, triangular cusps except on lower interior teeth, and a relatively thick root with nearly vertical margins.

facts.statement: Isurolamna inflata is the earliest and most gracile species within the genus.
facts.quote: Isurolamna inflataThis is the earliest and most gracile species.

facts.statement: Isurolamna inflata lived in North Africa, Europe, and North America during the Late Palaeocene and Early Eocene.
facts.quote: It is known from the Late Palaeocene (Selandian/Thanetian) and Early Eocene (Ypresian) of North Africa, Europe, and North America.

facts.statement: Isurolamna bajarunasi is a robust species found mainly in Kazakhstan during the Mid-Late Eocene.
facts.quote: Isurolamna bajarunasiKnown mainly from the Mid-Late Eocene (Bartonian-Priabonian) of Kazakhstan, this species is more robust than I. inflata but less so than I. gracilis.

facts.statement: Isurolamna gracilis is the most robust species in the genus and is known from Western Europe during the Early Oligocene.
facts.quote: Isurolamna gracilisThis species is known from the Early Oligocene (Rupelian) of Western Europe, and is the most robust species in this genus.

facts.statement: Isurolamna vandenbroeki is a rare species from the Early Oligocene found in Northwestern Europe and Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Isurolamna(?) vandenbroekiThis is a rare species from the Early Oligocene (Rupelian) of Northwestern Europe and Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: Isurolamna schoutedeni lived during the Late Early Ypresian stage of the Eocene epochs.
facts.quote: It lived in between the Late Early Ypresian stage, in Eocene epochs.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding whether Isurolamna vandenbroeki should be kept in its own genus or placed within Isurolamna, though many authors follow the diagnosis placing it in Isurolamna.
facts.quote: There is debate whether this is warranted or not but many subsequent authors have followed this diagnosis, particularly Cappetta (2012).
